subject: The Outsource Heist: How a $30,000 agency build was replaced with 140 lines of code
html:
Hey,

Three days ago, you joined this list to strip away manual overhead. Today, I want to share a raw financial breakdown from a client audit last month.

A founder spent $30,000 and 3 months with a traditional software agency to build an internal data routing pipeline. When we opened the repository, we found bloated Docker containers, unmonitored cron jobs, and $450/month in idle cloud server bills.

We killed the entire repository. Replaced it with an event-driven serverless worker, Edge KV storage, and direct API webhooks. Total code: 140 lines. Total setup time: 4 hours. Monthly cloud bill: $0.00.

This is what agencies don't want you to calculate: they sell headcount and billable hours; you buy margins and protocol-level speed.

If you're still burning capital on idle VMs or oversized databases, check out our baseline infrastructure stack over at wenboom.com. If you want to optimize your backend storage, we personally deploy on this zero-idle-cost database protocol.

subject: The Spreadsheet Trap: Why your manual workflows are a silent tax on scale
html:
Hey,

Most operators believe they have an operations problem. In reality, they have a state-management disaster disguised as Google Sheets.

When your team spends 15 hours a week copying webhook payloads, updating CRM rows, and manually triggering follow-up emails, you aren't paying for labor—you are paying a silent, compounding tax on human error.

At 10,000 inbound events per month, polling APIs manually will crash your response time and burn out your team. In our core pipeline, we handle inbound leads via webhook-driven asynchronous queues. Sub-millisecond response time, $0 overhead.

To handle high-deliverability communications without paying enterprise tax, we rely entirely on this developer-first email protocol. It plugs directly into serverless functions and guarantees delivery before your customer closes their tab.


Reply directly with your current stack setup. How many manual steps does an inbound lead take before getting a response in your system?
